🤖 Comment from Codex working with Leo:

Decision D018, revision 1: the compiler represents randomization through the existing doLog field.

Agreed that opted-out subjects must skip randomized allocations. The compiler decision assigns classification to the backend; the edge keeps the existing evaluator predicate.

Behavior — the distinction we are preserving
Allocation Compiler contract Opted-out subject in immediate mode
Ordinary percentage split or completed experiment that still randomizes doLog=true Skip.
Partial percentage enrollment doLog=true Skip.
Deterministic completed ordinary winner May use doLog=false Remains eligible.

This deliberately enables exposures for ordinary randomized allocations. Existing experiment, canary, bandit and holdout logging requirements remain. Future mode retains its strict-before cutoff; unknown activation excludes conservatively. Correct activation coverage/backfill is still needed.

Native validation — local checks for 939db39e16
  • The edge Go, Rust JSON/archive and Fastly suites pass; the native receipt is tied to this commit by the published-source binding.

theorem immediate_excludes_randomized_allocations (existingExposure : Bool) :

Legacy immediate Boolean experimentation_opt_out: true.
Future mode Named future mode plus normalized UTC cutoff.
Cutoff fraction .5 / .1234 / .000 .500 / .123400 / no fraction.
Equivalent numeric offset or nanosecond cutoff Preserve the exact instant.

Clients compare instants rather than requiring the sent and acknowledged strings to be identical.

  • Literal assertions exercise both encodings and both delivery paths, including offsets, zero fractions and nanoseconds.
  • Removing the serialized cutoff now fails the targeted test; the negative controls preserve the failure and restoration.
  • The final Fastly suite passes 244 tests with 9 existing ignores. The native receipt and published-source binding connect those results to the published patch. This is local evidence, separate from CI and deployment.
Sneak preview — turning review decisions into reusable, checked contracts

The reusable record in draft FFE test-data PR #55 connects D008, revision 2, a checked model theorem, the existing semantic oracle cases, and the linked validation history.

theorem future_requires_mode_and_matching_instant (ack : AckBoolean) (mode : AckMode)
    (cutoff : AckCutoff) :
    acknowledges .future ack mode cutoff = true ↔
      mode = .future ∧ (cutoff = .equal ∨ cutoff = .equivalent) := by
  cases ack <;> cases mode <;> cases cutoff <;> simp [acknowledges]

Within the acknowledgement model, future mode requires the future marker and an equal or equivalent cutoff instant. A boolean alone is insufficient.

The published model-validation receipt records this theorem among 53 audited statements, alongside 313 semantic and 36 operational cases. These are existing model results, not new executions for this formatting update. The model abstracts normalized-instant equality; the native literal tests cover actual serialization. The central PR remains a draft; broader adoption is a separate decision.

Stage Required behavior or prerequisite
